candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus XIX.8 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

Sinai wrapped in fire and smoke is, for Ephrem, the OT diptych of Pentecost: there the fire descends on a mountain and the people may not come near; here the fire descends on heads and tongues so that the people themselves become the mountain. Tewahedo reads Ex 19:18 and Acts 2 as the before-and-after of the divine fire — the same fire that thundered now rests on the believer without consuming.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.
